questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the language of the country was something I was proficient in, that the courses available seemed interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university welcoming and organization along with the housing prices detract from the overall experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. Most information was distributed via different emails, instagram posts and random events. It was very difficult to get a general overview.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a bus service to the school from the airport, along with student guides walking around the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I asked several times for a schedule or plans of what would happen for the coming weeks, but I was told no such thing existed, and that I should just "check instagram", where I needed to follow several different accounts, which would post events at random times. This was not very conducive for planning anything.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Several different residences.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Depended on the residence.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is extremely expensive, but it is practically the only option, since finding housing in Dublin is very difficult.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Student housing is distributed via a prioritizing list. So a prospective student would put their 1st, 2nd and 3rd priority for housing, yet there is no guarantee of getting a room in any of the prioritized residences. So it is entirely likely that a student would be assigned a housing option way outside of their price range. In order to first get assigned housing, a student has to pay 400 EUR which counts as a deposit, and there is no way to see which rooms are available before paying this fee. If you choose not to move in, UCD keeps those 400 EUR. In summarization: There are almost no other options beyond student housing, there is no way to see what student housing is available, one has to pay 400 EUR to get assigned housing without guarantee of the assigned housing being financially viable. Given that UCD profits from their student housing, it seems like they have a vested interest in keeping such a system, which favors the landlord and not the renter. Finally, upon moving into the housing UCD sent out a demand for 1000 EUR additional in deposit, despite explicitly stating that the 400 EUR paid is the full deposit. It took me my entire exchange to finally get this extra charge waived, but it did not foster a more positive view of the experience. All in all I feel that my experience with UCD housing really fostered a negative impression of the university and generally detracted from my experience there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The demands werent clear for what courses could be taken simoultaneously, and I didnt know until after I had arrived if the courses I had chosen beforehand were actually available, which ment I had to restructure my entire course structure and chose new courses, and apply for approval again. This is due to UCD not announcing what courses I was actually signed up for until a week before classes begun.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a lot of work, without time to ever fully engage in any one course.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: The level varied wildly, some courses I could do the coursework for a week in one or two hours, others took +10 hours, yet all of them are supposedly 5 ECTS.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot less student interaction, it was not particularly engaging.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The clubs and activites were the absolute highlight of my stay there, and greatly contributed to my social life and cultural engagement.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every kind imaginable, too many to list.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend the kickboxing society, which I was part of as it was both socially and personally developing for me.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend exploring the wicklow mountains, the cliffs of Moher, Galway and generally seeing Dublin and the local area like Dun Laoghaire, Blackrock and Howth.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, I think Irish people in general are more straightforward and warm than Danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I would really recommend two things:
Joining different societies and engaging with them.
Regularly going to the pub with a group of people, as this is the primary socialising spot in irish life.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it very challenging that irish people can be honest to the point of rudeness sometimes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I very much appreciated the warmth inherent in the irish culture, everyone was always willing to talk to you and I found that strangers would often strike up conversation.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Housing is expensive, seriously.
Engage in societies and clubs.
UCD bureaucracy is very decentralized and disorganised.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, enganging with irish culture, exploring a new country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely the academic workload and the price of housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.answer: Yes
